openings.claim: A removable lateral stop joint may resist sliding without the corner compression associated with opposite-corner lift.
openings.delta: Change the load carrier from seal friction under downward preload to hatch edges bearing against supplied-strip stops. Cut and drill only the strips; use bolted, rubber-padded removable rim clamps to support the stops, with vertical release clearance. Nearest rival: a padded hold-down joint relying on friction.
openings.prediction: With adequate clamp purchase and stop stiffness, edge restraint should limit displacement without tightening the left corner. The rival predicts that reducing preload restores sliding, while raising preload can reproduce opposite-corner lift. Equivalent displacement and lift across configurations would not discriminate; stop slip or opposite-corner lift defeats the proposed separation of lateral restraint from compression.
openings.probe: First use ruler inspection to establish accessible rim purchase, bolt reach and a stop arrangement locating the marked position while permitting full hatch removal. If these are absent, park the design. Fabricate at most two configurations: edge restraint and padded hold-down. Give each ten opening cycles; measure closure position, reopening time and new seal tears. Perform pulls after cycles one and ten, then one additional closure/pull with the stipulated right-contact card per configuration: six total trials. Record displacement and opposite-corner lift before and during each 20 N pull. Remove or relocate every rim component outside the full marked opening during opening; retain recoverability with the supplied cord. Stop fabrication if the ninety-minute allowance cannot accommodate both configurations.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits removable clamps and unobstructed release; this is unprovided.
Supplied strips, six bolts and pads can form sufficiently stiff stops without altering hatch or trough.
Cord routing and the twenty-minute observation allowance permit the stated cycles and measurements; verify rather than assume.
Seal protection must be checked after each cycle; visible tearing fails the hard constraint.

assessment: One speculative opening. It preserves the intended outcome but feasibility remains unresolved because rim attachment geometry and carrier capacity are unspecified. The dimensional check is a resource gate, not performance evidence; the cycle/pull comparison is a probe, not deployment.
